recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-11084 unless the Security WG later decides to change the CRUDE terminology itself.
issue_request: FHIR-11084 was a Published FHIR-core security technical correction. Although the submitted wording proposed changing CRUDE to CRUD, the final Not Persuasive with Modification resolution kept CRUDE and required explaining it as "(Create, Read, Update, Delete, Execute)" in the security.html Authorization/Access Control section.
initial_application: The RBAC/ABAC narrative was introduced by b40621eca169 with the unexplained phrase "the CRUDE events". Commit d6bec27176add2738ac0b05bd3dddcc177ab67ff, whose subject explicitly lists GF#11084, changed source/security.html to "the CRUDE (Create, Read, Update, Delete, Execute) events", directly applying the final resolution.
additional_context: source/hierarchy.xml lists security.html as the Security page under Security and Privacy, and current source/security.html still contains the parenthetical under Authorization/Access Control. Later nearby text maintenance did not remove or contradict the explanation. Jira, Zulip, and Confluence searches found no later decision that changes the FHIR-11084 conclusion.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The reconciliation published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch because the current source already implements the final Jira decision.
